title: The Spirit of truth (John 16:12–15)
hook: I have many things to say but you cannot bear them now

segments.voice: Yesterday, friends: the ones who are told everything. Your line was friends, not servants.

A good doctor doesn't read you the whole chart in the first five minutes. A good parent doesn't explain everything about death to a four-year-old at bedtime. A good teacher doesn't start calculus on the first day of algebra. Not because they're hiding something, but because there's an order to understanding. Some things you can only carry when you're ready. Jesus has just told his friends he gave them everything he heard from the Father. Now, still at the table, he says something that sounds like the opposite.
screen: `NOT THE WHOLE CHART AT ONCE.` → `AN ORDER TO UNDERSTANDING.` → `IT SOUNDS LIKE THE OPPOSITE.`

segments.voice: In the Douay-Rheims: "I have yet many things to say to you: but you cannot bear them now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth." So which is it? Has he told them everything, or not? Both, in a way. Everything has been given in him, but they can't carry it all yet. Bear is a carrying word, the kind you'd use for a heavy load. It's honest about the disciples: men who, within hours, will fall asleep in the garden and run. Jesus doesn't pretend they're ready. So he promises the Spirit of truth, who will teach them, or in the Greek, guide them, lead them along the way, into all the truth. Not dump it on them. Walk them into it. And the Spirit, Jesus says, won't bring a new message of his own. He'll take what is mine and show it to you. Catholics hear in this promise the Church's long, slow understanding of what it received. The Second Vatican Council taught that the understanding of what has been handed down grows over time, through contemplation, study and the experience of believers. In the nineteenth century John Henry Newman, now a canonized saint, wrote a whole book on how doctrine develops, the way a living thing grows up without turning into something else. Not new revelation, the Church says, but deeper understanding of what was given. Not yet, but coming.
screen: `YOU CANNOT BEAR THEM NOW.` · `HE WILL GUIDE YOU INTO ALL TRUTH.` · `NOT NEW: WHAT IS MINE, SHOWN.` · `NEWMAN: DOCTRINE GROWS LIKE A LIFE.` · then, large: `THE SPIRIT OF TRUTH.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you don't understand yet, about your faith, your life, a person, a loss, and don't try to solve it. Imagine setting it on a table in front of you: not thrown away, just set down to come back to later. If you pray, leave it there with Jesus's promise, he will teach you all truth; if you don't, simply let it rest on the table.
Truth. Jesus's promise that the Spirit will guide his friends into the truth they can't yet carry. Today's word.
Your line: not yet, but coming. Some things wait until you can carry them. Day five hundred twenty-three, done.

howItsDone: Catholics pray to the Holy Spirit for understanding, especially at Pentecost and before study or decisions, often with the traditional prayer "Come, Holy Spirit."

chat.says: If Jesus told his friends everything, why promise the Spirit would teach them more?
options: They couldn't bear it all yet. The Spirit guides them into it, showing what is his.
Because Jesus left things out, so the Spirit brings a brand-new message.
Because the disciples forgot most of it, so he had to start over.
chat.meaning: Everything was given in Jesus, but they couldn't carry it yet. The Spirit takes what is his and shows it, step by step.

Spirit of truth.meaning: Jesus's name for the Holy Spirit, who guides into all truth

Second Vatican Council.meaning: the Church council that taught understanding grows over time

John Henry Newman.meaning: a nineteenth-century saint who wrote on how doctrine develops

canonized.meaning: officially declared a saint by the Church
